findings.body: previousTaskIdRef tracks the previous task ID and prevents focus changes unless the ID explicitly changes, safely handling React 18 StrictMode double-invokes.
findings.title: Focus preservation

findings.body: Focus is reliably moved to the ritual Start/Pause button using primaryActionRef when the active task changes.
findings.title: Focus transitions

findings.body: The effect safely skips focus calls when currentTaskId is null, preventing fights with completeTask's headerRef.current?.focus().
findings.title: HeaderRef conflict avoidance

findings.body: The TaskSequencer.focusPreservation.test.tsx correctly uses <React.StrictMode> to prove focus isn't stolen on initial mount.
findings.title: Test coverage

findings.body: Changes are tightly scoped to the focus preservation requirements. No secrets or scope creep detected.
findings.title: Scope check

remaining_risks: The implementation depends on standard synchronous React state updates for focus. Rapid, concurrent task transitions could potentially cause a race condition, though unlikely in normal user interaction.
structured_output.summary: The implementation correctly uses previousTaskIdRef to prevent focus stealing during StrictMode double-invokes. Task transitions appropriately move focus to the ritual Start/Pause button. The completeTask function handles a null currentTaskId without conflicting with headerRef. Tests validate this behavior. No scope creep or secrets were introduced.
